messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: elevated SERVFAILs observed from multiple public resolvers for eu-central/eu-west geodns records. Triggered paging to on-call (Ryan).

Ryan: taking pager. Paging @Liz @Miguel @Carla. I'll own comms/coordination.

Liz: ack. My synthetic checks show sudden spike in SERVFAIL and timeout on authoritative responses from our Cloudflare zone in eu-central. TTLs weren't the issue; authoritative is returning SERVFAIL intermittently.

Miguel: can you share a trace/dig and the probe timestamps? Need to know if it's EDNS or AXFR related.

Liz: paste from a probe lambda (eu-central-1):
```
$ dig +nocmd @1.0.0.1 api.redwood-eu.example.com ANY +noall +answer +comments
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54321
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
;; SERVER: 1.0.0.1#53(1.0.0.1) (udp)
```
No authoritative answers returned.

Raj: CS reporting an uptick in EU customer errors (503s) for the last ~8 minutes. Not all customers, seems client-side resolution dependent.

Carla: infra note: if traffic shifts to our global pool we'll see higher egress and possibly higher cold-cache latencies. Prep scaling if we pivot traffic.

Zoe: drafting status for status.redwood.ai. Need impact blurb: "Intermittent DNS resolution failures for some EU customers; we are failing over DNS to mitigate and investigating root cause with provider." Any recommended phrasing?

Ryan: include: affected regions (EU Central, EU West), mitigation in place (authoritative failover + temporary CNAME fallback), and that some customers may experience increased latency. ETA unknown until provider confirms.

Miguel: suggestion for immediate mitigation (non-destructive):
1) Create temporary CNAMEs for critical api hostnames pointing to api.redwood-global.example.com with low TTL.
2) Update Route53 geo records to prefer a secondary authoritative NS set (our alternative hosted zone) for eu regions.
3) Open/attach dig/traceroute logs to Cloudflare case.

Liz: I'm seeing partial recovery after redirecting a canary subdomain to global CNAME (canary.api-redwood-eu). That suggests the issue is with authoritative answers served by Cloudflare edges in those regions.

cf-support: (via support thread) We are aware of a partial resolver/edge DNS cluster degradation across EU POPs. Engineers are investigating. Could be a memory leak under high query load.

Ryan: let's run the canary plan at scale. Miguel, enact CNAMEs + Route53 geo changes. Keep TTL to 30s. Carla, stand by to scale global pool by +25%. Liz, monitor resolution graphs and client error rates. Zoe/ Raj, prepare customer comms and CS playbook.

Miguel: applying CNAME changes for critical prefixes now. Sample command: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z-HOSTEU --change-batch '{
  "Comment":"temporary CNAME failover to global for EU due to resolver flap",
  "Changes":[{
    "Action":"UPSERT",
    "ResourceRecordSet":{
      "Name":"api.redwood-eu.example.com.",
      "Type":"CNAME",
      "TTL":30,
      "ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"api.redwood-global.example.com."}]
    }
  }]
}'
```
Applied to ~20 critical entries.

Carla: scaling global edge pool +25% now. Watching CPU and connection queues. No alarms firing yet but 95th latency up ~35ms.

Liz: probe graph: SERVFAIL rate drops ~80% after CNAME application; remaining errors likely from resolver caches still holding bad NS/A records.

Zoe: posted preliminary status update. Legal checked wording. Sending to Sales+CS.

cf-support: update: mitigation applied to affected edge resolvers, rolling restart scheduled for the cluster. Estimated full normalization 20-45 minutes.

Ryan: good. Keep failover in place until we get confirmation and at least 60 mins of stable probes. Miguel, capture change IDs and attach to incident ticket. Add rollback steps (remove CNAMEs and restore original geo records).

Miguel: change-batch IDs: CB-2244, CB-2245. Ticket with CF: CF-888222 opened. All artifacts uploaded (dig traces, probe timestamps, applied change-batches).

Raj: CS: we've flagged high-touch EU customers and offered direct circuit to support. No Dedicated customers reported data-plane issues; this appears solely DNS resolver related.

Carla: infra observation: global pool CPU rose 18% post-failover, autoscale absorbed without dropping below SLO. Keeping buffer for now.

Liz: probes green for 14 minutes. No new customer tickets in last 10m. Some resolver caches still showing old NS records; will decay with TTL.

cf-support: final update: we've completed rolling restarts and applied mitigations to the EU resolver cluster. Monitoring for regression; please advise when you want to revert your DNS changes.

Ryan: we'll wait 60m stable then coordinate revert. Zoe will update status with "mitigation in place, provider applied fixes" and expected revert timeline.

Zoe: status updated. Sent customer follow-ups and internal summary.

Miguel: preparing post-incident timeline and assigning postmortem owner (Miguel) and write-up owner (Zoe). Including exact change-batches and dig traces in the ticket.

incident-bot: Incident state -> Mitigating. INC-2026-0789.

Ryan: handoff plan: I'll remain on until 30m stability achieved post-provider confirmation. If all green, I'll hand to next on-call (Miguel) for postmortem and archival. If regression, we re-escalate.

Carla: leaving autoscale buffers for 24 hours. Will remove after PM review.

Liz: probes stable 30m. No new errors. Ready for revert when you give the go.

Miguel: scheduling revert window in 10m. Revert will be: remove temporary CNAMEs and restore authoritative geo A records with original TTLs. Rollback command prepared and attached to the incident ticket.

Ryan: thanks team. Good coordination. I'll update the incident status to "Recovering" and then to "Resolved" after revert completes and 1 hour of green metrics. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state -> Resolved (mitigated) pending postmortem. INC-2026-0789. Thread will be archived after 3h.
